text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.6% today to $136.27, continuing a sharp two-week decline of nearly 10% that began right after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th. The stock has shed $18 in less than two weeks, suggesting investors reacted negatively to those results—though the earnings details aren't specified in the available data, the timing of the selloff points directly to that disclosure as the trigger.

The broader oil and gas sector is also facing headwinds from the political landscape. A Democratic sweep in the midterm elections has shifted the outlook against fossil fuels and toward renewable energy, while persistent geopolitical tensions with Iran add uncertainty to crude supplies. Oil prices remain elevated (U.S. crude at $99.64/barrel), but that hasn't arrested the stock's decline, indicating that profit concerns from the earnings report and longer-term energy policy risk are outweighing near-term price support.
